evals.name: api-behavior-lookup
evals.prompt: does tokio's spawn_blocking have a thread limit? hitting weird stalls in my worker pool where tasks just sit there for like 30s before running
evals.expected_output: Direct answer that spawn_blocking uses a bounded blocking-thread pool (default max 512, configurable via max_blocking_threads), citing the official tokio docs with a deep link + quoted line. Should connect the limit to the observed stall symptom.

assertions.text: Cites at least one official source (docs.rs/tokio.rs/github.com/tokio-rs)
Includes at least one verbatim quoted line from a source, not just a paraphrase
Cited URLs deep-link to a section/anchor or specific page, not a site root
No links to disallowed sources (w3schools, geeksforgeeks, medium, tutorialspoint); any Stack Overflow link is explicitly labeled as a lower-confidence community fallback
Opens with the direct answer, not a preamble or a plan of what it will do
States the actual default blocking-thread cap (512) and names the max_blocking_threads builder option
Connects the thread cap to the user's reported symptom (tasks queueing/stalling ~30s), rather than answering the API question in isolation
Archive file written with question/date/stack frontmatter (with_skill runs only)

evals.name: spec-rfc-semantics
evals.prompt: whats the actual difference between 409 and 422, my api returns 409 for validation errors and a reviewer flagged it
evals.expected_output: Answer grounded in RFC 9110 (409) and RFC 4918 (422), with section-level deep links and verbatim quoted definitions. Should confirm the reviewer is right and say which code to use for validation failures.

assertions.text: Cites at least one official source (rfc-editor.org / ietf.org / httpwg.org / MDN)
Includes at least one verbatim quoted line from a source, not just a paraphrase
Cited URLs deep-link to a section/anchor or specific page, not a site root
No links to disallowed sources (w3schools, geeksforgeeks, medium, tutorialspoint); any Stack Overflow link is explicitly labeled as a lower-confidence community fallback
Opens with the direct answer, not a preamble or a plan of what it will do
Cites RFC 9110 for 409 specifically (not the obsolete RFC 7231/2616)
Attributes 422 to RFC 9110 (core HTTP since 2022, 'Unprocessable Content') rather than treating it as WebDAV-only legacy from RFC 4918
Gives a clear verdict on the reviewer's flag rather than hedging both ways
Archive file written with question/date/stack frontmatter (with_skill runs only)

evals.name: multi-part-migration
evals.prompt: i need to migrate our vite config from v5 to v7, whats going to break
evals.expected_output: Breaking-change summary spanning both the v5->v6 and v6->v7 migration guides, citing official vite migration docs with section anchors. Should surface Node version requirements and default-behavior changes. Broad enough to justify fanning out to subagents.

assertions.text: Cites at least one official source (vite.dev / vitejs.dev / github.com/vitejs)
Includes at least one verbatim quoted line from a source, not just a paraphrase
Cited URLs deep-link to a section/anchor or specific page, not a site root
No links to disallowed sources (w3schools, geeksforgeeks, medium, tutorialspoint); any Stack Overflow link is explicitly labeled as a lower-confidence community fallback
Opens with the direct answer, not a preamble or a plan of what it will do
Covers BOTH migration hops (v5->v6 and v6->v7), not just one
Names the Node.js version requirement change as a breaking item
Flags that the user's actual current version should be confirmed from package.json/lockfile before acting
Archive file written with question/date/stack frontmatter (with_skill runs only)
